text: Given valid X-Ramp-Client-Id/X-Ramp-Client-Secret headers, when the agent calls tools/list, then it receives exactly the 7 v1 tools with non-empty descriptions and parameter schemas; GET /health returns 200 {"status":"ok"} even when Ramp is mocked as unreachable.
Given a POST /mcp request missing X-Ramp-Client-Secret, when any tool is called, then the server returns 401 naming the missing header, and the mocked Ramp API receives zero calls.

Given valid credentials, when ramp_list_transactions is called with from_date/to_date/department_id against a mocked multi-record response, then only records matching every filter are returned, each with id/amount/currency/state/merchant/card_holder/department present.

Given a 2-page mocked list response on a v1 list tool, when the agent re-calls the tool with the first page's next_cursor, then it receives page 2 with no overlap with page 1, and the last page's next_cursor is null.
Given a transaction_id the mock does not recognize, when ramp_get_transaction is called, then it returns a structured not_found error envelope, not an unhandled exception or 500.
Given card_type="physical" or "virtual", when ramp_list_cards is called, then it calls the matching Ramp endpoint (/cards/physical or /cards/virtual) only and returns only cards of that type.
Given valid credentials and an email filter, when ramp_list_users is called, then only the matching mocked user record is returned.
Given valid credentials and a state filter, when ramp_list_reimbursements is called, then only matching mocked records are returned.
Given valid credentials and vendor_id + payment_status filters, when ramp_list_bills is called, then only matching mocked records are returned.
Given valid credentials and a name filter, when ramp_list_vendors is called, then only the matching mocked vendor record is returned.

Given Ramp responds 429 to a proxied call, when the tool call completes, then it returns a structured error envelope with code=rate_limited and the upstream trace id, without raising and without a silent retry loop.

Given two tool calls arrive concurrently with two different Client-Id/Client-Secret header pairs, when both execute, then each caller receives only its own mocked tenant's data and the token cache ends up with two distinct keys.
README.md Connector section and Header credential table are present and correct.
steps: Open README.md in the delivered repo
Check the Authentication headers table lists X-Ramp-Client-Id and X-Ramp-Client-Secret with where-to-obtain text
expect: Connector paragraph is verbatim-identical to the reference file; both headers are documented with where to obtain them in the Ramp Developer Portal.
